agree.reason: The memo gives clear math, checkpoints and a fallback, and it handles the ad sales person respectfully, so most of the board could vote yes. But the two ad-background members are never told why ads must end entirely rather than run alongside membership, and they would likely push back on that.

honest.reason: It is mostly careful: it presents full replacement as a goal, admits a $30,000 first-year gap, and leaves a placeholder for pilot retention. However, it says the ad decline happened 'over two years' when it happened in one, it adds an unsupported claim that ads slow the site, and it says one other newsroom 'shows the model works at our scale', which overstates a single example.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures for 875 members, 6% of the list, 1.5% conversion and about $50,000 in year one are all correctly derived. But it spreads the 36% fall across two years, so its projection of about $65,000 understates what continuing at last year's rate would give (about $54,000), and the case for change ends up weaker than the facts support.

right_comparison.reason: It does describe the status quo as a shrinking source and projects it forward. But by treating a one-year 36% collapse as a two-year trend, it makes keeping ads look roughly twice as safe as the facts show.

qualification.reason: The checkpoints are dated and numbered, and the June 30 one comes with a concrete consequence: below 450 members, staff will return with options including bringing back some ads. The March and December checkpoints have no stated consequence if they are missed.

objections.reason: It answers the staffing worry well and gives a midyear point at which ads could come back. It does not answer the sales-minded members' likely question of why the newsroom can't keep shrinking ad revenue while membership builds.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted board memo, about one page, with a recommendation up front and a clear requested action at the end. It may run slightly over a page once the placeholders are filled in.
